judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

R. Suresh Kumar, J.:— The prayer in this writ petition is for a Writ of Mandamus, directing the second Respondent to consider the petitioner's representation dated 21.06.2019 and thereby direct the 4th respondent to adhere the peace committee proceedings dated 07.08.2017 while conducting the temple festival namely Arulmigu Sri. Ayyanar Sri. Karuppasamy Temple, Vellore, Viralimalai Taluk, Pudhukottai District within the time stipulated by this Court.

2. Heard Mr. D. Sadiq Raja, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Mr. C.M. Mari Chelliah Prabhu, learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondents 1 to 3. Since no adverse order is going to be passed against the 4th respondent, notice to him is dispensed with.

3. With the consent of both sides, this writ petition is disposed of at the admission stage itself.

4. Regarding the conducting of festival called “Kuthirai Eduppu” at the village temple viz., Arulmigu Sri. Ayanar, Sri. Karuppasamy Temple at Vellore village, Viralimalai Taluk of Pudhukottai District, there had been a peace committee meeting at the instance of the revenue people on 07.08.2017 and in that meeting, both the rival groups i.e., the group headed by Muthukumar, the 4th respondent herein and the group headed by one Nalluchamy, participated among others and in the said peace committee meeting, unanimous decision has been taken to the following effect:

5. Pursuant to the said decision taken in the peace committee meeting, from 2017 onwards, the festival is being conducted on rotational basis. It seems, in the year 2017, the group of Muthukumar, 4th respondent herein conducted the festival in consultation with the legal heirs of 5 people mentioned in para 3 of the decision of the said meeting and in the next year, the group of Nalluchamy conducted the festival. Like that, this year, it is the turn of the 4th respondent to conduct the festival and the date of festival also has been fixed to be conducted on 30.08.2019 between 5.00 p.m. and 10.00 p.m. and as has been agreed upon by the parties in the peace committee meeting held on 07.08.2017, all the legal heirs of 5 persons mentioned in para 3 of the decision of the said meeting should have been consulted and in this regard, it is the grievance of the petitioner that, he is the one of the legal heir of one late Ayyavu Pillai, who was among the 5 persons mentioned in para 3 of the minutes and he has, according to the petitioner, not been consulted by the 4th respondent and therefore, if he is consulted along with other legal heirs as agreed upon by the parties in the minutes of the said peace committee meeting, the petitioner's grievance would be redressed.

6. I have heard the learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the official respondents, who would submit that, insofar as the festival is concerned, it is scheduled to be conducted on 30.08.2019 and the procedure already agreed upon by the parties concerned in the minutes recorded in the peace committee meeting would be followed. However, insofar as the forthcoming Kumbabishekam of the temple, some dispute arose between the two groups and therefore, in that regard, the revenue people planned to have a peace committee meeting separately.

7. I have considered the said submissions made by both sides and having regard to the said facts and by taking into account the aforesaid documents referred to above, this Court is inclined to pass the following order:

“The 2nd and 3rd respondents shall ensure that the 4th respondent shall consult the legal heirs of the 5 persons mentioned in para 3 of the minutes of the peace committee meeting held on 07.08.2019 and in that process, the petitioner, being one of the legal heir of late Ayyavu Pillai, also shall be consulted by the 4th respondent as in the case of other legal heirs and accordingly, taking into account his suggestion also, the festival shall be conducted by the 4th respondent with the help of other village people. In this regard, the representative from the 2nd and 3rd respondents office shall visit the village prior to 30.08.2019 and ensure that such consultation process is taken place, whereby, the 4th respondent consults the petitioner also being one of the legal heir of the 5 stalwarts of the village concerned, who are no more. If the said exercise is completed before 30.08.2019, this Court feel that there shall be no further impediment to conduct the festival by the 4th respondent and in this regard, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, would submit that, the petitioner would not have any objection for the 4th respondent to conduct the festival this year as the turn comes only to him as per the arrangement and his only grievance is consultation to be made by the 4th respondent with the petitioner. Therefore, the above said arrangement alone shall be ensured by the 2nd and 3rd respondent offfice.”

8. With this observation and direction, this writ petition is disposed of. No costs.
